title: Builder project registration - what buyers should verify before booking
p1:
A builder saying “the project is registered” does NOT mean you should book immediately.

One small verification can save you from a very expensive mistake.
p2:
Many buyers check only whether the project has a registration number. But registration is not the same as approval of every promise the builder has made.

The real question is: does the registered project match what you are being offered?
p3:
Before paying a booking amount, verify the project’s registration details on the relevant RERA authority’s website. Check the registered project name, developer, location, approved completion date, sanctioned plans, and the units or phases actually covered by the registration.

Here’s the part many buyers miss: marketing material can sometimes describe amenities, timelines or specifications more broadly than the registered project documents.

So don’t rely only on the brochure or sales pitch. Compare the promise with the official record.

A registration number is a starting point—not a substitute for due diligence.
conclusion: Before booking a property, would you check the builder’s RERA records yourself, or rely on what the salesperson tells you?
